results.name: The buying company orders stock from the selling company; prices default to cost + 10 % mark-up; the seller is told
Only the selling side approves (not the requester); prices can be agreed on approval; buyer is told
The seller dispatches the order: stock is picked from the seller's bins (split over bins) into a transfer owned by the buyer on arrival
An order larger than the seller's stock cannot be dispatched (nothing moves)
Receiving issues a tax invoice from seller to buyer for what arrived, at the agreed prices, with 15 % VAT
The rest arrives: a second invoice; the order is completed; owners changed exactly by what was invoiced
A transfer between companies without an order gets an automatic order; a written-off shortage is not invoiced
An issued invoice can never be changed or deleted, even by the database owner
Seller issues a partial credit note (damaged drum), then records payment; buyer cannot
Each side sees its own documents; others see nothing; anonymous callers are refused
Invoice export: seller sees sales lines, buyer purchase lines, credit notes negative; totals agree
Stock integrity stays clean after inter-company trading; anonymous access sanity holds
